title: Separate the incompatibilist condition from necessary alternative possibilities
author: Worldview Sorter editorial draft
currentBehavior: AHI103 and AHI104 alone support construct-AH14 on Quick and Standard; disagreement with AHI104 opposes the broad conditional even when AHI103 and AHI105 favor it.
proposedBehavior: A new version of construct-AH14 uses AHI103@1 and reverse-keyed AHI105@1 as its two evidence opportunities, excluding AHI104@1 from that broad rule. New Quick and Standard versions replace AHI104@1 with AHI105@1. Preserve AHI104@1 for historical and separately scoped analysis.
rationale: The current pair can double-count closely related fixed-prior-condition formulations and confuse a necessary-alternatives view with the broader incompatibilist condition. Preserve missing and mixed states when the remaining evidence does not agree.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: If a choice is causally determined by the complete prior state and laws, it cannot be genuinely free.
neighboringViews: Compatibilism that permits free action under determinism
Source incompatibilism that does not require alternative possibilities
Belief that determinism is actually true
Denial that free will is possible under any conditions
nonEntailments: The respondent believes determinism is true
The respondent believes any person has free will
The respondent endorses libertarian free will
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: AHI104 asks about necessary alternative possibilities and overlaps heavily with AHI103, while AHI105 directly presents a nearby compatibilist sufficient condition. Quick and Standard omit AHI105.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: Accounts of free will differ over alternative possibilities, sourcehood, and moral responsibility. The broad incompatibility conditional should not identify one of those narrower theories.

sourceClaims.claim: The core incompatibilist conditional concerns whether a deterministic world can contain free will, independently of whether determinism is true or free will is actual.
Alternative-possibilities and sourcehood arguments are distinguishable; rejecting the former does not by itself reject every incompatibilist account.

alternatives: Keep AHI104 as a second independent unit; rejected because its content is too close to AHI103 and it can misclassify source-based incompatibilism.
Add a new free-will question immediately; deferred because AHI105 already supplies a nearby alternative for this narrow conditional, while broader theories remain unmeasured.
respondentImpact: Some frozen-pilot supported or mixed states would become leaned toward, supported, or opposed under a separately labeled current reinterpretation. Quick and Standard route content and affinity coverage reports must be recalculated. No raw answer changes.
historicalCompatibility: Keep model-release-1.0.0, the exact three item revisions, and progressive-depth-1.0.0 unchanged. Publish any approved correction as new model and route artifacts and a new model release; do not rewrite old administrations or share snapshots.

release.migration: No raw-response rewrite. Historical results use model-release-1.0.0; any new rule and routes use new versioned artifacts and are presented as a current reinterpretation when applied to old answers.
